item.text:
**Reused evidence**
REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0001"],"lenses":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10"]}

**New evidence**
- 2022’s first clear cross-border strike on Iraq is the March Erbil missile attack. It shows direct coercive force rather than restraint.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran attacks Iraq's Erbil with missiles in warning to U.S., allies","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-03-14","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/03/14/uk-iraq-security-erbil","claim":"Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for a dozen ballistic missiles fired at Erbil; the attack was presented as retaliation for an Israeli air raid in Syria, and Kurdish authorities said a civilian was injured.","locator":"article body, paragraphs describing the attack and casualties","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire report with contemporaneous attribution and casualty reporting.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 event","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Iran's state security apparatus under Khamenei's ultimate authority, though not a personal order transcript.","contrary_evidence":["IRGC framed the strike as retaliation, not aggression.","No American personnel were hurt, so the immediate material harm was limited relative to later 2022 attacks."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.4","2B.6","2B.10"]}
- A late-March Reuters report tied the Erbil strike to broader regional energy and Israel-linked rivalry, undercutting Iran's defensive framing.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran struck Iraq target over gas talks involving Israel - officials","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-03-29","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/03/29/us-iraq-iran-usa-israel","claim":"Iraqi and Turkish officials said a nascent Iraqi Kurdistan gas export plan involving Israeli participation helped trigger Iran's strike on Erbil; the IRGC described the strike as a message and retaliation for Syria.","locator":"lines 667-674 of the article body","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire with specific claim, sourcing to regional officials, and a clear chronology close to the event.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 event and retrospective explanation published within the same month","ruler_attribution":"Indirect attribution to Iranian state policy and IRGC decision-making under Khamenei's strategic umbrella.","contrary_evidence":["This is an anonymous-sourced reconstruction, not a court finding.","Iran was responding to a perceived Israeli challenge, so the piece does not by itself resolve defensive necessity."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.6","2B.10"]}
- UNAMI’s May briefing is useful because it combines harm, attribution, and a note that dialogue was still open.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Briefing to the Security Council by SRSG Jeanine Hennis-Plasschaert","publisher":"United Nations in Iraq / UNAMI","publication_date":"2022-05-17","url":"https://iraq.un.org/en/182221-briefing-security-council-srsg-jeanine-hennis-plasschaert-17-may-2022","claim":"The SRSG said Iran's missile attack on Erbil killed civilians, including a little girl, but also noted that Iraq and Iran were engaged in dialogue and did not wish to escalate the issue.","locator":"lines 101-105 and 127-130 of the briefing text","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary UN field-mission briefing, contemporaneous and directly specific to the attack and the diplomatic context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 follow-up to the March attack","ruler_attribution":"The attack is attributed to Iran within the UN diplomatic record; that is a state-action attribution under Khamenei's authority rather than a personal speech transcript.","contrary_evidence":["The same briefing acknowledges ongoing Iraq-Iran dialogue, which is the main restraint/peace point in the 2022 record.","This is a diplomatic briefing, not a legal finding on command responsibility."],"lenses":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10"]}
- By late September, Iran was openly justifying attacks on Kurdish opposition sites as border security.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran's Guards launch artillery attack on militants in Iraqi Kurdistan","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-09-25","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/09/25/iran-iraq-artillary","claim":"Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched artillery attacks on Iranian militant opposition bases in northern Iraq and said the operations would continue to ensure border security and punish terrorists.","locator":"article body, quoted IRGC statement and surrounding paragraphs","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire with direct operational attribution and the Guards' stated rationale.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 event during the Mahsa Amini protest wave","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to the IRGC under Iran's top security hierarchy, which Khamenei ultimately oversees.","contrary_evidence":["The official rationale is a self-serving security claim, not independent proof of necessity.","The targets were opposition bases in another sovereign state."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.5","2B.6","2B.10"]}
- The September 28 cross-border campaign is the clearest 2B negative in 2022 because it paired explicit attribution with civilian deaths.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran says it fired 73 ballistic missiles at Kurdish groups in northern Iraq","publisher":"The National / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-09-28","url":"https://www.thenationalnews.com/mena/iraq/2022/09/28/iran-attacks-groups-in-northern-iraq-in-new-drone-bombing-campaign/","claim":"Reuters reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired 73 ballistic missiles at Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq; Iraqi Kurdish authorities said at least nine civilians were killed and dozens were wounded.","locator":"article body and casualty summary near the headline sections","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters feed with explicit numerical and casualty claims from the same-day attack.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 event at the height of the protest crackdown","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to the IRGC under Khamenei's strategic authority, even if the decision chain is not laid out in the article.","contrary_evidence":["Iran framed the strike as counterterrorism against Kurdish militants.","Casualty counts varied across local reports, so the exact death toll is not perfectly settled."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.6","2B.10"]}
- The clearest Russia-related evidence is Iran's own acknowledgment that drones went to Moscow in 2022, even if it tried to push the transfer before the invasion date.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran acknowledges drone shipments to Russia before war, Kyiv says Tehran is lying","publisher":"Investing.com / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-11-05","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iran-acknowledges-drone-shipments-to-russia-before-war-kyiv-says-tehran-is-lying-2933668","claim":"Iran's foreign minister said a small number of drones had been supplied to Russia months before the February 24 invasion and denied continued supply, while Reuters noted Russia had used the drones against power stations and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine.","locator":"article body around the foreign minister's quoted remarks","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire carried contemporaneous acknowledgement from Iran's foreign minister, which is unusually direct evidence.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 conduct and public acknowledgment","ruler_attribution":"Indirect but strong attribution through Iran's foreign minister speaking for the regime under Khamenei's authority.","contrary_evidence":["Iran denied that the transfers continued into the war.","The report does not prove a direct Khamenei order or timing beyond 'months before' the invasion."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.6","2B.10"]}
- The EU sanctions decision is a strong independent corroborator of Iranian UAV support to Russia.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Ukraine: EU sanctions three individuals and one entity in relation to the use of Iranian drones in Russian aggression","publisher":"Council of the European Union","publication_date":"2022-10-20","url":"https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2022/10/20/ukraine-eu-sanctions-three-individuals-and-one-entity-in-relation-to-the-use-of-iranian-drones-in-russian-aggression/","claim":"The Council said three Iranian individuals and one Iranian entity were sanctioned because of their role in the development and delivery of UAVs used by Russia in its war against Ukraine.","locator":"opening paragraphs of the press release","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary EU sanctions text, explicit about the reason for designation and the Russia-Ukraine context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 sanctions response to the drone issue","ruler_attribution":"Attribution is to Iranian state-linked actors, not directly to Khamenei personally, but the action sits inside the system he heads.","contrary_evidence":["Sanctions target listed persons/entities, not the Supreme Leader by name.","The EU press release is a legal-political response, not a forensic finding on the entire chain of command."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.10"]}
- Treasury's November action adds more detail on production, transfer, and harm to civilians.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Treasury Targets Actors Involved in Production and Transfer of Iranian Unmanned Aerial Vehicles to Russia for Use in Ukraine","publisher":"U.S. Department of the Treasury","publication_date":"2022-11-15","url":"https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy1104","claim":"Treasury said firms were involved in the production or ongoing transfer to Russia of Iranian UAVs that Russia used in attacks on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, and identified Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center as responsible for Shahed-series UAV production.","locator":"opening section and the 'Iranian UAV Producer' section","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary U.S. sanctions notice with concrete findings, named entities, and mission-specific details.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 conduct and sanctions response","ruler_attribution":"Indirect attribution to the IRGC aerospace ecosystem under Khamenei's rule.","contrary_evidence":["This is a sanctions determination by the U.S., not an international adjudication.","It names firms and the IRGC aerospace force, not Khamenei personally."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.5","2B.8","2B.10"]}
- The final 2022 Iraqi-Kurdish strike shows the same pattern continued after the protest wave intensified.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran strikes dissident sites in Iraqi Kurdistan, two dead - officials","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-11-15","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/11/15/iraq-security-kurdistan","claim":"Reuters reported that rockets and drones hit Iranian Kurdish party headquarters in Iraqi Kurdistan, killing at least two people and wounding ten, and said the Revolutionary Guards had been attacking dissident bases since the Mahsa Amini protests began.","locator":"article body around the casualty count and IRGC attribution","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire with same-day reporting and direct attribution to the Guards.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 late-year conduct","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to the IRGC under Khamenei's security hierarchy.","contrary_evidence":["Iran described the targets as terrorist groups and framed the operation as security-related.","This is still a media report, not a judicial finding."],"lenses":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.6","2B.10"]}

**Search and rejection summary**
I screened roughly 30 documents across Reuters syndications, Euronews Reuters wires, UNAMI/UN Iraq material, U.S. Treasury, EU Council, State Department briefings, IranWatch mirrors, Al Jazeera, The National, Washington Post, and several 2023-2024 retrospective sources.

Rejected or deprioritized:
- Duplicate syndications of the same Reuters wire when they added no new fact.
- Out-of-period material, especially 2023 border-security arrangements and 2024 retrospectives.
- Broad regional background pages that did not add Khamenei- or 2022-specific international conduct.
- State Department page fetches that were technically blocked; I used Reuters republishers instead where the same claim was accessible.
- Sources that only repeated the local-prior baseline without adding ruler-specific conduct.
- Purely domestic repression material, because that belongs mainly in Chapter 3B unless it is tied to cross-border conduct or proxy use.

**Remaining gaps**
- Direct Persian-language 2022 Khamenei or IRGC transcript spelling out the rationale for the March, September, or November Iraq strikes.
- Better primary documentation of the command chain from Khamenei to the IRGC operations, especially for 2B.5 and 2B.9.
- More direct, contemporaneous evidence on the full 2022 Russia drone-transfer pipeline, especially whether shipments continued after the invasion or were confined to prewar transfers.
- More explicit evidence of restraint or ceasefire activity that is truly ruler-attributed, rather than general UN dialogue language.
- Additional search would help on attribution and proxy-control questions, but the current evidence already supports a clearly negative 2022 international-peace picture centered on repeated cross-border coercion and support for Russia's war effort.
